palette.notes: Measured 33 colours, 2 ramps, median ramp hue shift 4.3, ramp length 16.5. Skin and shadows built from a lavender-blue ramp; accents in pastel pink, yellow, teal hair strands; screen mixes with UI chrome.

lighting: Flat, graphic: skin is shaded with blue-violet tones on a white base, little directional light. Black line art does most of the form.
silhouette: Profile of a girl's face with mechanical headphone/gear shapes behind her; strong profile line (nose, lips) and big eye read clearly.

motion.timing: Speedpaint screen recording, not an animation: code reads 486 changes, 24.28 changes/s, hold median 16.7 ms, on 0.5s, which is brush strokes and UI flicker, not drawings.

texture: Clean pixel line art (clean_pixels true, dither 0.0008), flat fills with a few shade bands; transparency checkerboard visible as layers are filled.
camera: Screen capture of the Aseprite canvas; zoom and pan change between sheet frames (canvas reframed from full face to an eye close-up at 9.17 s).

acting.enters: No character acting. The image is built line by line: sketch, line art, flats, shading, hair colours.
acting.acts: Not a performance; the reveal of the drawing is the story. Caption says changes the artist forgot to record get skipped.
acting.depth: Single canvas; zoom-ins to the eye give a close-up beat inside the process.

techniques: speedpaint reveal: line art, then flats, then shading
cool lavender ramp for skin shading instead of warm skin tones
pastel accent strands on a mostly monochrome base
zoom in on the eye mid-process as a detail beat
transparent checkerboard background as a visual 'work in progress' cue
feel: black line art + lavender skin ramp + pastel hair accents + stroke-by-stroke reveal = satisfying build-up
for_fred: Not a motion reference. One idea to borrow: reveal Fred's sprite being drawn (outline, then flats, then shading) as a 1-2 s intro or Easter egg, ending on him blinking to life. Keep the reveal fast; a 25 s build is too long for a reel beat.
